identification.summary: Sandman is a name SentinelLabs gave to a cyberespionage cluster it described in September 2023, working with QGroup GmbH, that targeted telecommunications service providers in the Middle East, Western Europe and South Asia [S1][S5]. Its signature tool is LuaDream, a modular backdoor built on the LuaJIT platform, which is rare in APT malware [S1][S4]. In a December 2023 follow-up, SentinelLabs, Microsoft and PwC reported that LuaDream and the KEYPLUG backdoor were observed in the same victim environments and that Sandman shares infrastructure management practices with the cluster Microsoft calls Storm-0866 and PwC calls Red Dev 40 [S2][S3].
identification.firstObserved: SentinelLabs reported the activity in September 2023 [S1][S5]. Coverage says compilation timestamps and a string artifact suggest the malware dates to the first half of 2022 [S5]; other coverage describes the observed intrusions as lasting a few weeks in August 2023 [S4]. Treat the exact start as unverified.
identification.notes: Sandman is the SentinelLabs-assigned name; the Storm-0866 (Microsoft) and Red Dev 40 (PwC) names describe a related but separately tracked cluster, and the researchers state the attribution link is suggestive rather than conclusive [S2][S3]. Component counts for LuaDream differ between outlets (34 in Dark Reading, 36 in others) [S4][S5].

attribution.confidence: In September 2023 SentinelLabs could not tie the activity to a known actor and speculated the operators could be a private contractor or mercenary group [S5]. In December 2023 SentinelLabs, Microsoft and PwC described the cluster as China-based on the basis of overlap with KEYPLUG activity (Storm-0866 / Red Dev 40) [S2][S3]. The researchers said there is no evidence that LuaDream and KEYPLUG are developed by a single vendor and that the malware may be supplied through dedicated channels [S3]. The sources reviewed do not name a PRC government sponsor.
attribution.basis: Co-existence of LuaDream and KEYPLUG in the same victim environments, and shared infrastructure control and management practices with Storm-0866 / Red Dev 40 [S2][S3]. Storm-0866 / Red Dev 40 is described as a developing threat cluster primarily targeting entities in the Middle East and South Asia [S2][S3].

objectives: Cyberespionage against telecommunications providers. Reporting notes that the targeted workstations belonged to managers, which suggests interest in privileged or confidential information [S5]. Sponsor and tasking are not established in the sources reviewed.

sectors: Government entities (reported for the associated Storm-0866 / Red Dev 40 cluster, not Sandman itself) [S2][S3]
targeting.notes: SentinelLabs described victims across three continents [S4]. Secondary coverage states that the targeted workstations belonged to managers [S5]. Specific victim organizations and counts are not named in the sources reviewed.

capabilities.summary: LuaDream is a modular, multi-protocol backdoor built on LuaJIT; it exfiltrates system and user data and manages attacker-supplied plugins, and its design comprises dozens of components (34 or 36 depending on the outlet) [S1][S4][S5]. The staging chain loads the malware into memory and is designed to avoid detection [S1][S4]. Lua-based malware has been rare in the wild, with earlier examples including Flame, Animal Farm and Project Sauron [S3]. The KEYPLUG backdoor appears in the same victim environments [S2][S3].

campaigns.summary: Compilation timestamps and a string artifact suggest the malware dates to the first half of 2022; this is an inference from malware artifacts, not an observed intrusion [S5].

campaigns.summary: Coverage describes Sandman intrusions against telecom providers lasting a few weeks in August 2023, using LuaDream with in-memory staging [S4].

campaigns.name: SentinelLabs public disclosure of Sandman
campaigns.summary: SentinelLabs, with QGroup GmbH, publishes the Sandman profile and the LuaDream analysis; the actor is unattributed and a mercenary or contractor operator is speculated [S1][S5].

campaigns.name: Link to KEYPLUG / Storm-0866 / Red Dev 40
campaigns.summary: SentinelLabs, Microsoft and PwC report LuaDream and KEYPLUG in the same victim environments and shared infrastructure management with Storm-0866 / Red Dev 40, described as China-based [S2][S3].

diamond.adversary: Unattributed in September 2023, with a contractor or mercenary operator speculated [S5]; linked in December 2023 to a China-based KEYPLUG-using cluster (Storm-0866 / Red Dev 40), a link the researchers call suggestive [S2][S3].
diamond.capability: LuaDream LuaJIT modular backdoor, in-memory staging, KEYPLUG in the same environments [S1][S2][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Shared infrastructure control and management practices with Storm-0866 / Red Dev 40 [S2][S3]. Specific hosting and C2 details were not retrievable in the sources reviewed.
diamond.victim: Telecommunications providers in the Middle East, Western Europe and South Asia [S1][S5].
diamond.technology: Telecom networks hold privileged and confidential data of interest [S5].

gaps: Could not open the primary SentinelLabs reports (September and December 2023) or the Microsoft and PwC material; details rely on secondary coverage and search summaries.
No government sponsor is named in any source reviewed; the China-based description comes from vendor assessments and is described as suggestive.
Whether Sandman is a distinct actor or a customer of shared tooling is unresolved; researchers say malware may be supplied through dedicated channels [S3].
Component count of LuaDream is inconsistent across outlets (34 vs 36) [S4][S5].
Start date is uncertain (possibly 2022 versus August 2023 observations) and activity after December 2023 was not found.
No Microsoft actor-naming entry or MITRE ATT&CK group for Sandman was confirmed; the record's mitreGroupId remains empty.
Initial access vector, victim names and C2 indicators are not established in the retrieved sources.
Hive Pro and second Dark Reading sources were removed because their URLs could not be confirmed; DLL hijacking and pass-the-hash details were dropped.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Telecommunications provider networks, especially management workstations, are key terrain [S5]. STEP 2: The actor operates in the Middle East, Western Europe and South Asia and has used an uncommon LuaJIT framework that may evade signature-based detection [S1][S4]. STEP 3: Reported tradecraft is lateral movement to specific workstations with minimal interaction, then in-memory LuaDream with plugin-based collection [S1][S5]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued espionage against telecom providers in the named regions. MDCOA is use of telecom footholds for broader access to carrier-held data, an inference not stated in the sources.
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track telecom-sector reporting on Sandman, Storm-0866 and KEYPLUG together while keeping cluster boundaries separate [S2][S3]. (2) Authorities: telecom networks are largely commercial or allied-owned, so hunting and mitigation on them depend on partner and provider consent. (3) Mission assurance: DoD reliance on commercial and host-nation telecom links in the named regions makes provider compromise a mission risk. (4) Coordination: share indicators through DC3 and allied and commercial partners, and treat attribution as unsettled given the vendor caveats [S3].

provenance.importedSummary: First disclosed in 2023, the Sandman APT is likely associated with suspected China-based threat clusters known for using the KEYPLUG backdoor, specifically STORM-0866/Red Dev 40. Sandman is tracked as a distinct cluster, pending additional conclusive information. A notable characteristic is its use of the LuaDream backdoor. LuaDream is based on the Lua platform, a relatively rare occurrence in the cyberespionage domain, historically associated with APTs considered Western or Western-aligned.
